title: Speech runtime ownership and concurrency
summary: Speech is provider-neutral ooRexx TTS/STT. One channel is one ordered lane; separate channels execute concurrently. Resident Python providers remain behind Macrospace and are independent per lane by default.
invariants: Speech owns TTS/STT semantics, channel state, stream lifecycle, audio profiles, duplex orchestration and dynamic Speech intentions.
One SpeechTTSChannel or SpeechSTTChannel is an ordered lane. Different channel objects may execute concurrently through separate ooRexx activities.
One resident Python Macrospace provider object per speech lane is the default. Sharing provider objects requires separate backend qualification.
Bulk PCM does not cross the scalar Macrospace marshaller. Streaming uses bounded PCM artifacts/chunks while descriptors and events cross Macrospace.
SIP owns signalling and call state; RTP owns codecs, packetisation and media timing; local audio backends own devices; Speech composes through decoded PCM seams.
Layered Audio and Storage retain authoritative audio/material identity. Speech may consume transient materialisations but does not replace their authority.
qualification: dev10 r13196 regressions proved concurrent batch/streaming TTS/STT, local audio and duplex-session behavior.
dev12 independent r13196 cross-package qualification at commit e65b97548b7d444719726c8554a2cbc51621662d passed against SIP dev15 and RTP dev7; no network calls were made.
